newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end down on fears of crackdown.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end down on fears of crackdown.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index closed down 5.127 points or 6.35 percent to 75.558 points on Thursday on fears that the securities authorities would restrict mainland Chinese trading B shares, traders said.
Volume was 65.5 million shares worth $28.8 million.

The fears were sparked by news reports that local securities authorities in Shenzhen had launched a new crackdown on Chinese buying B shares by ordering brokerages to ensure that the money used for trading came from outside China, they said.
"The Shenzhen crackdown has triggered fears it will spread to Shanghai," said a trader. "Sentiment has been badly hurt."

Traders said another reason for today's fall was profit-taking after the surges of the past few weeks. The B index has risen 80 percent over the past month on expectations that Beijing would take measures to support the market.
"Profit-taking focussed on cheap shares which rose the most during the surges of recent weeks," a second trader said.
Shanghai Sanmao Textile was the biggest loser, plunging $0.072 or 20.11 percent to $0.286 on volume of 643,700 shares.
Shanghai Lianhua Fibre, which had surged 200 percent in recent weeks, was the second biggest loser, shedding $0.044 or 13.75 percent to $0.276, on heavy volume of 1.4 million shares.

Shanghai Diesel Engine, which listed an additional 85 million shares on Thursday, had the highest volume on inter-institutional trading, traders said. It lost $0.036 or 6.21 percent to $0.544 on volume of 6.0 million shares.

Shanghai's A share index closed down 70.491 points or 5.42 percent to 1230.831 points on a technical correction after repeatedly hitting three-year highs over the past few sessions, traders said. The SSE 30 blue-chip index lost 111.482 points or 3.64 percent to 2952.753 points.
Brokers said A share market sentiment was still good and the index would recover next week after the powerful correction.
